info.title: Trade Octane API
info.description:
Welcome to the updated Trade Octane API documentation.
This version marks our official migration to the Octane architecture. This upgrade replaces our legacy processing systems to deliver lower latency, higher throughput, and real-time trade execution.

post.summary: Authenticate a legacy Trade Octane credential.
Authenticate an FCEPL domain credential through single sign-on.
post.description: Verifies the domain credential with the corporate SSO provider and, only on success, resolves the matching Trade Octane account. Returns the same body as the standard login. Fails closed: if SSO is disabled or the provider cannot be reached, the call is rejected rather than falling back to any other check.

get.summary: Whether single sign-on is configured on this deployment.
get.description: Lets the client decide whether to offer an SSO button at all, instead of showing one that always fails. Reports a boolean and nothing else — no provider URL, no settings.

post.summary: End the session this access token represents.
post.description: Revokes the calling token for the remainder of its lifetime. Repeating the call with the same token returns 401, because the token is no longer accepted.

get.summary: The menu and sub-menu tree the signed-in user is granted, plus their role names.
The activity/spend/BRD count tiles and brand-wise tiles shown on the post-login dashboard.
Cursor-paged, searchable user directory.
get.description: Replaces the CreateUser.aspx grid. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1. Send the previous response's nextCursor as 'cursor'; a cursor is only valid for the search, status, sort and direction it was issued under. Supports If-None-Match for 304 revalidation.

post.description: Writes to both catalogues in one transaction and records a forced password change, so the new credential cannot be used until its holder changes it. Omit 'password' to assign the configured default; omit it necessarily when 'domainId' is set, since a federated account authenticates against Entra.

get.summary: One user by login name.
The 'Check' button: is this address taken, and what should the form be pre-filled with?
get.description: Checks the local directory first, then the corporate directory. Returns either the existing account or a creation suggestion. GET, not POST, because it is a lookup with no side effects — which also makes it cacheable and safe to retry.

get.summary: The filtered directory as a CSV download.
get.description: Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding. Honours the same search and status filters as the list endpoint.

post.summary: Activate an account in both catalogues.
Deactivate an account in both catalogues and drop its cached grants.
Clear the account lock set by failed sign-in attempts.

get.summary: The assignable role catalogue.
get.description: Replaces the chk_Roles checkbox list. Defaults to active roles only: a retired role grants nothing, because every read on the access path filters Roles.Status = 1, and the legacy screen offered all 43 including the 6 retired ones. Each role carries how many users hold it. Supports If-None-Match for 304 revalidation.

get.summary: Cursor-paged, searchable user/role mapping grid.
get.description: Replaces the grd_Details grid, which was unpaged and re-bound in full on every postback. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1. Send the previous response's nextCursor as 'cursor'; a cursor is valid only for the search, filters, sort and direction it was issued under.

get.summary: The filtered mapping grid as a CSV download.
get.description: Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding. Honours the same filters as the list endpoint.

get.summary: The roles one user holds, and the roles they could hold.
get.description: Has no legacy counterpart, and its absence is why the legacy screen could not revoke anything: selecting a user did not post back, so the checkbox list was never pre-checked with that user's current roles. 'assigned' includes retired roles the user still holds — real rows worth cleaning up — while 'available' offers only active ones.

put.summary: Set a user's roles to exactly this set.
put.description: The endpoint the legacy Save button should have been. Adds what is missing and revokes what is not listed, in one transaction. An empty roleIds array revokes every role. Idempotent: re-sending the same set writes nothing, returns added/removed empty, and generates no audit rows.

post.summary: Add roles to a user without revoking any.
post.description: The legacy Save semantics, minus its defects: the whole set is applied in one statement rather than one un-transacted insert per role, a role already held is a no-op rather than the error 'User Already Exists in Role.', and the response reports every role's outcome instead of one label overwritten per loop iteration.

delete.summary: Remove one role from a user.
delete.description: The grid's delete button. Both identifiers are route parameters; legacy read them out of rendered GridView cells, one of which it had deliberately hidden.

get.summary: The signed-in user's own account details.
get.description: Replaces the UpdatePassword.aspx page load. Returns login name, full name, email, whether a password change is due, and how old the current password is. It does NOT return the password: the legacy screen decrypted the stored credential into an unmasked textbox on every load.

put.summary: Change your own password, and optionally your name and email.
put.description: Replaces the Update Information button. The account changed is always the one the token identifies. 'currentPassword' is required when calling with a normal session token and ignored when calling with the restricted password-change token issued at first login. The new password may not repeat any of your last 5. The credential update and the password-history row are written in one transaction — see AccountSql for why splitting them can lock an account out entirely.

put.summary: Set another user's password, full name and email — the Change User Password screen.
put.description: Replaces ChangeUserPassword.aspx. Pick the account with the route's userId, send the password you want it to have, and optionally correct the full name and email in the same call. Populate the screen's picker from GET /api/v1/admin/users?status=Active and its fields from GET /api/v1/admin/users/{userId}. 'forceChangeAtNextSignIn' defaults to true; send false to reproduce the legacy behaviour, where the administrator went on knowing a working password for that account indefinitely. 'loginName' is accepted only to be checked — the legacy screen posted it into UPDATE Users SET User_ID = ..., renaming the primary key from inside a password dialog, and a value that differs from the route is refused rather than quietly dropped. Use PUT /api/v1/admin/account/password for your own account.

post.summary: Reset another user's password to the configured default.
post.description: The narrower sibling of PUT .../password: it assigns Administration:DefaultPassword rather than a password the caller chose, carries no profile fields, and always flags the account so the holder must replace the credential before it is usable for anything else. Send an explicit 'newPassword' only when the default will not do; prefer the PUT when you also need to correct the name or email. Legacy had no equivalent of this shape — ChangeUserPassword.aspx always required the administrator to invent a password, and Proc_Forget_Password mailed one in clear.

get.summary: Cursor-paged, searchable menu grid.
get.description: Replaces the grd_Menus grid, which was unpaged and re-bound in full on every postback. Filter by octane to see one application's items: Octane1 is the Administration 1.0 tree, Octane2 is Administration 2.0. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1; a cursor is valid only for the filters, sort and direction it was issued under. Each item reports whether it renders in the legacy menu and in the ported one — see activationMismatchCount.

post.description: octane is required and decides which application the item appears in. menuPage must end with '.aspx' — legacy declared that rule as a validator and then never checked Page.IsValid. activation defaults to Active, which is the fix for the legacy screen writing an empty string on every insert. A parent must be an existing top-level item in the same octane tree. The new item is reachable by nobody until it is granted through Access Control; requiresAccessGrant says so.

get.summary: The filtered menu grid as a CSV download.
get.description: Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding. Includes the grant counts and both render flags, so a spreadsheet of the menu can be filtered to the items nobody can reach.

get.summary: The icon names the menu can render.
get.description: The 24 Font Awesome 4 names the legacy ddl_Icons dropdown offered, so a client can build the picker without hard-coding them a second time. The list deliberately excludes "NULL": that was the placeholder option's value, and writing it stored the four-character string, which 13 rows still hold. Send null for no icon.

get.summary: One application's menu as the two-level tree it renders as.
get.description: The administrator's view of the whole tree — NOT what any given user can reach. GET /api/v1/access/menu is the access-filtered one. An item here may be reachable by nobody at all: 18 currently have no grant of any kind.

get.summary: One menu item.
get.description: The read behind the legacy select button, done properly. That button read fixed grid cell indices, so a re-sort between render and click loaded a different row — and it never populated Menu Page or the icon at all.

put.description: Legacy had no update: its select-then-Insert workflow created a duplicate instead, which is the likeliest origin of the 10 duplicate (name, octane) pairs in the table. This is a full replace — every field is written, and an omitted field takes its default rather than the row's current value. The one exception is activation, which is left as-is when omitted.

put.summary: Show or hide a menu item.
put.description: The reversible alternative to a delete, which this API deliberately does not offer: 2,821 user grants and 840 role grants reference this table with no foreign key, so a delete would orphan them silently. activation is required and accepts Active or Hidden only; an empty body is rejected rather than defaulted.

get.summary: The assignable region catalogue.
get.description: Replaces the chk_Regions checkbox list. Regions come from Centegy_SnDPro_DR.dbo.GEO_LEVEL6 — a different database, which is why no foreign key protects the mapping table and why codes must be sent back exactly as reported here. Defaults to active regions only, matching SP_Region_List's own ActiveInactive = 'Y' filter: 9 of the 16 are live. Each region carries how many users hold it. Supports If-None-Match for 304 revalidation.

get.summary: Cursor-paged, searchable user/region mapping grid.
get.description: Replaces the grd_Details grid, which was unpaged and re-bound in full on every postback. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1; send the previous response's nextCursor as 'cursor', and note that a cursor is valid only for the search, filters, sort and direction it was issued under. Unlike the legacy grid this shows every row: view_User_Region_Mapping filtered USERS.Active = 1 and hid 1,402 of the 1,991 mappings. Each row reports whether it actually grants anything.

get.summary: The filtered mapping grid as a CSV download.
get.description: Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding. Honours the same filters as the list endpoint and includes the user and region status columns, so a spreadsheet of coverage can be filtered to the dead grants.

get.summary: The regions one user covers, and the regions they could cover.
get.description: Has no legacy counterpart, and its absence is why the legacy screen could not revoke anything: ddl_User had no SelectedIndexChanged handler and no AutoPostBack, so selecting a user never pre-checked the list with what they already held. 'assigned' includes retired regions the user still holds — and any whose code no longer names a catalogue row — because those are real rows worth cleaning up; 'available' offers only live ones.

put.summary: Set a user's regions to exactly this set.
put.description: The endpoint the legacy Save button should have been. Adds what is missing and revokes what is not listed, in one transaction. An explicit empty regionCodes array revokes every region; an ABSENT regionCodes is rejected, so a malformed body cannot revoke by accident. Idempotent: re-sending the same set writes nothing, returns added/removed empty, and generates no audit rows. Revoking narrows the user's budget visibility and can remove them from the scheme approval pool.

post.summary: Add regions to a user without revoking any.
post.description: The legacy Save semantics, minus its defects: the whole set is applied in one statement rather than one un-transacted insert per region, a region already held is a no-op rather than the error 'Mapping Already Exists.', and the response reports every region's outcome instead of one label overwritten per loop iteration.

delete.summary: Remove one region from a user.
delete.description: The grid's delete button. The region code is a query parameter rather than a route segment because it is a tilde-joined path such as '1000~4000~1000~0040~0002~0002' — opaque, caller-supplied, and not something to embed in a URL path. This endpoint deliberately does NOT validate the code against the catalogue: a mapping whose region has been deleted is exactly the row that needs removing, and refusing it would make the cleanup impossible through the API that reports the problem.

get.summary: The assignable brand catalogue.
get.description: Replaces the chk_Brands checkbox list. Brands come from Centegy_SnDPro_DR.dbo.PROD_LEVEL6 — a different database, which is why no foreign key protects the mapping table and why codes must be sent back exactly as reported here. Defaults to active brands only: 16 of the 22. NOTE this differs from what legacy offered — SP_Brand_List filtered by 'has a master SKU' instead, which yielded 21 and silently excluded the one brand whose Code disagrees with its own PROD1~…~PROD6 concatenation. Each response carries hasMasterSku so that rule can be reproduced deliberately. Supports If-None-Match for 304 revalidation.

get.summary: Cursor-paged, searchable user/brand mapping grid.
get.description: Replaces the grd_Details grid, which was unpaged, unsearchable and re-bound in full on every postback — Get_User_Brand_Mapping took no parameters at all. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1; a cursor is valid only for the search, filters, sort and direction it was issued under. Each row reports whether its brand still exists and whether the row actually grants anything; danglingCount reports the whole-table figure, and danglingOnly=true lists exactly those rows.

get.summary: The filtered mapping grid as a CSV download.
get.description: The legacy screen had no export at all. Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, honours the same filters as the list endpoint, and includes the user and brand status columns — so danglingOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of the 233 rows that need cleaning up.

get.summary: The brands one user covers, and the brands they could cover.
get.description: Has no legacy counterpart, and its absence is why the legacy screen could not revoke anything: ddl_User had no SelectedIndexChanged handler and no AutoPostBack, so selecting a user never pre-checked the list with what they already held. 'assigned' includes retired brands the user still holds — and any whose code no longer names a catalogue row — because those are real rows worth cleaning up; 'available' offers only live ones.

put.summary: Set a user's brands to exactly this set.
put.description: The endpoint the legacy Save button should have been. Adds what is missing and revokes what is not listed, in one transaction. An explicit empty brandCodes array revokes every brand; an ABSENT brandCodes is rejected, so a malformed body cannot revoke by accident. Idempotent: re-sending the same set writes nothing, returns added/removed empty, and generates no audit rows.

post.summary: Add brands to a user without revoking any.
post.description: The legacy Save semantics, minus its defects: the whole set is applied in one statement rather than one un-transacted insert per brand, a brand already held is a no-op rather than the error 'Mapping Already Exists.', and the response reports every brand's outcome instead of one label overwritten per loop iteration.

delete.summary: Remove one brand from a user.
delete.description: The grid's delete button. The brand code is a query parameter rather than a route segment because it is a tilde-joined path such as '1000~4000~0070~0040~0005~0008' — opaque, caller-supplied, and not something to embed in a URL path. This endpoint deliberately does NOT validate the code against the catalogue: the 233 mappings whose brand does not exist are exactly the rows that need removing, and refusing them would make the cleanup impossible through the API that reports the problem.

get.summary: Cursor-paged, searchable grid of every direct menu grant.
get.description: Has no legacy counterpart — Access_Rights.aspx showed one user at a time, so 'who can reach this page' meant opening 545 users in turn. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1; a cursor is valid only for the search, filters, sort and direction it was issued under. Each row reports whether the grant actually confers access, whether a role already supplies it, and whether it is orphaned. orphanedCount and redundantCount are whole-table figures, not this page's.

get.summary: The filtered grant grid as a CSV download.
get.description: The legacy screen had no export at all. Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, and honours the same filters as the list endpoint — so deadOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of the grants that confer nothing.

get.summary: One user's access tree, direct grants, and effective access.
get.description: Replaces trv_Menu, and reports the three things it could not distinguish. directMenuIds is what this endpoint's writes control; roleMenuIds is what the user's live roles supply and PUT here cannot remove; effectiveMenuIds is the union filtered to active items — what AccessSql.EffectiveMenu resolves and what actually authorizes requests. Every tree node carries grantSource and the roles granting it. Send directMenuIds back unchanged for a guaranteed no-op.

put.summary: Set a user's direct menu grants to exactly this set.
put.description: The legacy Update button, as one transaction instead of a delete-everything followed by N unguarded inserts. An explicit empty menuIds array revokes every direct grant; an ABSENT menuIds is rejected, so a malformed body cannot revoke by accident. Idempotent: re-sending the same set writes nothing, returns added/removed empty, and generates no audit rows. The response's noLongerEffective names what the user can genuinely no longer reach — a revoked grant a role also supplies is not in it.

post.summary: Add direct grants to a user without revoking any.
post.description: Has no legacy equivalent — the only save available deleted everything first. Use this to grant one new screen without having to know, and echo back, everything else the user already holds. A grant they already have is a no-op rather than an error.

delete.summary: Remove one direct grant from a user.
delete.description: Also has no legacy equivalent: removing one item meant unchecking it and re-saving, which deleted and rewrote every other grant the user held and wrote an audit row for each. Returns 409 when the menu item is granted only through a role — removing it here would change nothing, and the response names the roles to edit instead.

get.summary: Cursor-paged, searchable grid of every role/menu grant.
get.description: Has no legacy counterpart — the screen showed one role at a time, so 'which roles grant this page' meant opening all 43 in turn. Keyset ('cursor') pagination, so page N costs the same as page 1; a cursor is valid only for the search, filters, sort and direction it was issued under. Each row carries the role's user count, so the reach of any grant is visible without a second call, and whether the grant confers anything at all. deadGrantCount is the whole-table figure, not this page's.

get.summary: The filtered role grant grid as a CSV download.
get.description: The legacy screen had no export at all. Streams RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, and honours the same filters as the list endpoint — so deadOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of the 108 grants on retired roles and the 48 on inactive menu items.

get.summary: One role's access tree, its granted set, and who it reaches.
get.description: Replaces trv_Menu, and adds the number the legacy page most conspicuously lacked: userCount and activeUserCount say how many people a change here would affect. orphanedMenuIds names children granted without their parent — invisible in the menu, still authorized by the API. Send menuIds back unchanged for a guaranteed no-op.

put.summary: Set a role's menu grants to exactly this set.
put.description: The legacy Update button, as one transaction instead of a delete-everything followed by N unguarded inserts. An explicit empty menuIds array revokes everything from the role; an ABSENT menuIds is rejected, so a malformed body cannot revoke by accident — on a role held by 83 people that is not an acceptable failure mode. Idempotent: re-sending the same set writes nothing and generates no audit rows. The response reports affectedUserCount and affectedUserIds.

post.summary: Add grants to a role without revoking any.
post.description: Has no legacy equivalent — the only save available deleted everything first. This is how a newly created screen is granted to a role without restating the 54 items the largest role already holds. A grant it already has is a no-op rather than an error.

delete.summary: Remove one menu item from a role.
delete.description: Also has no legacy equivalent: removing one item meant unchecking it and re-saving, which deleted and rewrote every other grant the role held and wrote an audit row for each — on ASM, 12 rows rewritten and 12 audit lines to remove one menu item. This endpoint does NOT check whether the role is retired: a retired role's grants confer nothing and are exactly the rows worth cleaning up.

get.summary: Where pending approvals are stuck, across every table and stage.
get.description: Has no legacy counterpart — the screen made you pick a role, a user, a table and a level before it would show anything, and answered for one person at a time. This answers 'where is work stuck' directly: one row per holder per stage, with the holder resolved against USERS. stuckOnly=true returns just the queues whose holder cannot act on them, which today is 15,419 of the 19,644 pending approvals. totalPendingRows and stuckPendingRows are whole-set figures, not this page's.

get.summary: The queue census as a CSV download.
get.description: The legacy screen had no export at all. RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, honouring the same filters as the census — so stuckOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of every queue that needs re-routing.

get.summary: The rows a re-route would move — the preview.
get.description: Replaces btn_Search_Click, with the difference that this preview is binding: its totalCount is what POST /api/v1/admin/re-route requires back as expectedCount, and the write refuses if the queue has changed since. Legacy's grid was decorative — the Re-Route button recomputed the predicate at click time and moved whatever matched then. The holder is matched as the stored string, so a placeholder value such as 'Please Select' previews like any login name.

post.summary: Move every pending approval at one stage from one holder to another.
post.description: The Re-Route button, as a guarded transaction. expectedCount is required and comes from the preview; the UPDATE runs, its row count is compared to it, and the whole thing rolls back with a 409 if they differ — so a queue that moved in between is never half-applied. currentHolder is matched as the stored approver string, which is the only route to the 13,239 rows holding a dropdown placeholder rather than a person; newHolder is always validated against USERS, because the point is to hand work to someone who can act on it. Every call writes one audit row — legacy wrote none.

get.summary: The year, month, scheme-type and region pickers.
get.description: Replaces the four Load* calls Page_Load made on first render. The year list is in ascending order and contains only years — legacy's was ordered placeholder, current, +1, +2, -1 because LoadYears inserted at index 1 twice, and its first item's value was its own label, so leaving it selected sent that label into b.[Year] = as a bare term and the page silently did nothing.

get.summary: Refresh: which tables hold budgets, who owns them, who may receive them.
get.description: Refresh_Click ran three queries across one postback and left the products to a fourth. All three lists come back here in one call. The owner list is a LEFT join to USERS where legacy used an inner join with no ACTIVE test — so it surfaces the owners legacy could not list at all, and stuckShellCount says how many shells sit with someone who cannot act on them.

get.summary: The products holding budgets in a chosen dimension table.
get.description: Replaces cbl_table_SelectedIndexChanged. currentOwner is optional here, where legacy required it and so dead-ended whenever the owner dropdown was empty. The product code is the concatenated PROD1~..~PROD6 form, which is what the shell search filters on — legacy's picker used each table's stored Code column while its grid used the concatenation, so the picker could offer a value the grid would never match.

get.summary: Search: the budget shells matching the filters.
get.description: Replaces LoadBudget and Search_txtbx_TextChanged, which were the same body copied twice. Legacy's search predicate had an operator-precedence bug that let every row with a null description and a null shell code through ALL the filters, and its term was never escaped so a typed % matched everything. Both call sites also guarded the rebind with 'if rows > 0', so a search matching nothing left the previous result set on screen for the user to tick and transfer. totalCount is the uncapped count; resultsTruncated says the scope exceeded the server's row cap and the filters need narrowing.

get.summary: The search results as a CSV download.
get.description: The legacy screen had no export. RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, honouring the same filters as the search — so ownerStatus=NotAUser or driftedOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of exactly the budgets that need reassigning.

post.summary: Transfer: move budget ownership from one person to another.
post.description: The Transfer button, as one guarded transaction. Legacy looped the grid's checkboxes and per row issued two UPDATEs on two separate connections with no transaction, swallowing every exception and reporting success regardless. Here shellCodes names the selection explicitly, expectedCount is required, and if the number of those shells actually owned by currentOwner differs, the whole transaction rolls back with a 409 and nothing moves in either table. BUDGET_APPROVALS is updated only for the shells that actually moved and only where INITIATED_BY still names the outgoing owner, so approvalRowsUpdated below shellsTransferred is the ownership drift, not a failure. newOwner is always validated against USERS — legacy's dropdown could write its own '>>SELECT<<' placeholder into the ownership column. One audit row per transfer, not one per shell.

get.summary: Accounts and their recorded resignation dates.
get.description: Replaces the grid, whose WHERE clause defeated its own Active filter — 'where Active = 1 and user_id like … or FULL_NAME like …' means '(Active AND id) OR (name)', so a search by name returned deactivated accounts the dropdown above could not select. Filters are explicit here. suspectOnly=true lists the dates the legacy screen may have stored with day and month transposed; recorded=NotRecorded answers 'who has left and has not been recorded', which the grid showed but could not filter on.

get.summary: The same list as a CSV download.
get.description: The screen had no export. RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, honouring the same filters — so suspectOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of every date that may need correcting, with the alternative reading in its own column. Dates are written yyyy-MM-dd, deliberately not the dd-MM-yyyy the legacy screen used.

get.summary: One account's resignation state.
get.description: Replaces the grid's Edit button, which selected the account in the dropdown and then blanked the date box — hiding the currently recorded date, which is the one fact needed to decide whether to change it.

put.summary: Record or correct an account's resignation date.
put.description: The Update button. The date is sent as yyyy-MM-dd and bound as a parameter, so nothing is parsed from text — legacy pasted dd-MM-yyyy into the SQL and let the server interpret it under the connection's DATEFORMAT, which silently transposed day and month whenever the day was 12 or below. The outcome is the update's own row count, so an id that matches nothing is a 404 rather than a success message. The response carries the value that was replaced, and says whether the account can still sign in — recording a resignation does not deactivate anyone.

delete.summary: Clear an account's recorded resignation date.
delete.description: Legacy had no way to do this, which compounds its date bug: a date stored with day and month transposed could be overwritten but never removed. Clearing the date box and clicking Update wrote an empty string, which SQL Server stores as 1900-01-01 — a wrong date rather than no date. A separate verb rather than a null in the PUT body, so a client with a serialisation bug cannot erase a date it meant to write.

get.summary: The year, month and claim-type pickers.
get.description: Replaces the three Load* calls Page_Load made on first render. The year list is in ascending order and contains only years — legacy's LoadYears inserted at index 1 twice, producing placeholder, current, +1, +2, -1, and each dropdown's placeholder was a live value because a ListItem built from a bare string uses it as both text and value.

get.summary: Who owns activities in a period and claim type.
get.description: Replaces the claim-type postback. Each owner carries a status and an activity count, neither of which legacy showed: it bound FULL_NAME straight off a LEFT join, so an owner that is not an account rendered as a blank but selectable dropdown entry, and it never tested ACTIVE at all. stuckActivityCount says how many activities sit with someone who cannot work them.

get.summary: Who a given owner's activities may be transferred to.
get.description: Replaces GetActivityUsersNew — everyone sharing a role with the current owner — minus its duplicates (it had no distinct, so a candidate sharing two roles appeared twice) and minus the current owner themselves, who shares all of their own roles and so was always offered as a recipient. When the owner has no roles at all, which is the case for every owner that is not an account, the list widens to all active accounts and 'widened' says so — legacy's dropdown was simply empty, leaving the orphaned activities unmovable.

get.summary: The activities owned by one person — the grid, and the search.
get.description: Replaces Get_Users_Activity, called from two copied blocks. Legacy's approval join carried 'and sa.Initiated_By = pb.USER_ENTRY', so an activity whose chain had already drifted matched nothing and rendered with blank approval columns — looking like an activity with no chain rather than an inconsistent one. Here the join is on the key alone and the disagreement is reported as ownershipDrifted; driftedOnly=true lists just those. The search covers the marketing-plan code, the sequence id and the description, escaped — legacy searched the sequence id alone, unescaped, so a typed % matched everything.

get.summary: The same activities as a CSV download.
get.description: The legacy screen had no export. RFC 4180 CSV with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel opens it in the right encoding, honouring the same filters — so driftedOnly=true gives a ready-made worksheet of every activity whose ownership and approval chain disagree.

post.summary: Transfer: move activity ownership from one person to another.
post.description: The Transfer button, as one guarded transaction across three tables in two catalogues. Legacy issued three UPDATEs on three separate connections with no transaction, once per checked row, swallowing every exception. Each activity is named by BOTH mpCode and seqId — legacy matched on the sequence id alone, and unquoted against a varchar column. expectedCount is required; if the number of named activities actually owned by currentOwner differs, everything rolls back with a 409. If the second catalogue's pb_setup matches a different number of rows, that is also a rollback and a distinct 409 — it means the two databases already disagree about these activities. approvalRowsUpdated below activitiesTransferred is ownership drift, not a failure. One audit row per transfer, not one per activity.

get.summary: Search the frequency configuration grid.
Scheme groups available to the prior-month editors.
Scheme types belonging to one or more selected group keys.

get.summary: One dispatch note, from SAP and from Trade Octane's own records.
get.description: Replaces the AutoDA Status button. 'period' is the month as yyyy-MM. Returns SAP's delivery lines with an 'eligibility' verdict on each — the reason a line would or would not be posted, which the legacy grid could not show — plus 'localStatus', the Status_Flag counts that say whether this dispatch note has already reached Salesflo. 'sapAvailable' is false when no SAP connector is wired; the local status is still returned.

post.summary: Start an Auto-DA release for a month. Returns 202 with a run id.
post.description:
Replaces the AutoDA Release button. Pulls the month's invoices and deliveries from SAP, reloads the two staging tables, builds the candidate set and posts one payload per dispatch note, recording each outcome. The work happens in the background: poll the returned statusUrl. Only one Auto-DA release may be in progress at a time — a second request is refused with 409 and the id of the run that holds the slot, because two concurrent releases post every dispatch note twice.

'dryRun' defaults to TRUE. A dry run reads SAP, reloads the staging tables and reports the exact payload it would send for every dispatch note, without calling Salesflo, without touching Status_Flag and without writing audit rows. Live releases additionally require Integration:AutoDa:Enabled, which is off by default until the staging-to-permanent step missing from the migrated source has been identified — see the slice notes.

get.summary: SAP's current sale-allowed status for one or more batches.
get.description: Replaces the Batch Status Summary button. Repeat 'batchNo' for several batches — the legacy screen took one textbox and pasted it into a CHARG IN ('...') filter expression, so asking for two meant typing A','B and relying on that injection. Send the raw SAP batch number: the composite 'batchCode' (batch plus SKU suffix) that the pipeline and Salesflo use is derived and returned alongside it. Note the 'lookbackDays' in the response — every batch lookup pulls that much batch master data out of SAP before filtering, which is why it is not fast.

post.summary: Push batch status to Salesflo. Returns 202 with a run id.
post.description:
Replaces the Batch Release button. For each batch/SKU pair it upserts SKUBatch_AutoDA_SAP and posts the status, recording every outcome — the legacy version overwrote its status message on each iteration, so only the last pair's result was ever visible, and its audit insert was commented out so nothing was recorded at all. Poll the returned statusUrl. Only one batch push may run at a time.

'dryRun' defaults to FALSE here, unlike the Auto-DA release: this pipeline has no open questions against it, and a dry run would only report what it was about to do.

get.summary: Recent integration runs, newest first.
get.description: Without per-item detail — ask for a single run to get that. Runs are held in memory and are lost when the service restarts; the durable record of what was posted is in Activity_Logs, one row per dispatch note.

get.summary: One run, with the outcome of every dispatch note or batch it touched.
get.description: Poll this after a 202. 'state' moves Queued -> Running -> Succeeded, CompletedWithFailures, Failed or Cancelled. 'items' carries one entry per dispatch note (or batch/SKU pair) with the platform's own response, which is the detail the legacy screen discarded — its batch release overwrote its status message on every iteration, so only the last one was ever visible.

Bearer.description: Paste the raw token — no 'Bearer ' prefix. Use the token from POST /api/identity/login for /me; use an Entra ID access token for /admin/users.
